title: Top-down and bottom-up processing

draft.title: Top-down and bottom-up processing
card: processing starts with the raw sensory data from the stimulus. The brain builds a perception from these features, with little help from what the person already knows.
processing starts with what the person already knows, expects or has experienced. The brain uses this to interpret the sensory data.

Bottom-up processing is more important when a stimulus is new or unfamiliar, because there is no past knowledge to draw on. Top-down processing is more important when the stimulus is familiar, unclear or incomplete.
Most perception uses both at once. The senses supply the data, and knowledge helps make sense of it.
draft.remember: Bottom-up starts with the stimulus. Top-down starts with what you already know.

opts: Reading a smudged word by using the sentence around it
Noticing a sudden bright flash of light in a dark room
Feeling the heat of a stove when you touch it
Seeing the edges and colours of a shape you have never seen
a.why: The reader uses knowledge of language and context to work out an unclear word. The other options start with the sensory data itself and need no prior knowledge, so they are bottom-up.
a.clue: Which one relies on what the person already knows?

b.q: Tariq visits a city for the first time and sees a bird unlike any he has met. He studies its colours, shape and call to form an idea of it. Which process is mainly at work?
opts: Bottom-up, because he has no past knowledge to use
Top-down, because he is forming an idea of the bird
Top-down, because he is paying close attention to it
Bottom-up, because he is using more than one sense
b.why: The bird is new, so Tariq builds his perception from its features. That is mainly bottom-up processing. Forming an idea is not the same as top-down, which needs prior knowledge or expectations to guide it.
b.clue: Is there any past knowledge about this bird to draw on?

a.best: Reading a smudged word by using the sentence around it

b.best: Bottom-up, because he has no past knowledge to use

problems.detail: The why says the other options 'need no prior knowledge'. The card says bottom-up works 'with little help' from what the person knows and that most perception uses both kinds at once. The why should be softened to match, for example 'rely mainly on the sensory data'.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clear right answer. The only issue is that the why for (a) says the other options need 'no' prior knowledge, which overstates the card's 'little help' and its point that most perception uses both kinds of processing.
